answer: The cheapest real defence: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because spiral only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, ledge is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any cedar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
